pairs.reason: Both are clean and correct, and both handle float rounding and a clock that steps back. Implementation 1 is also thread-safe, rejects an infinite rate, and its tests cover concurrency and client errors, which tips it slightly despite the unneeded properties.

Implementation 1 is leaner and handles float tolerance and backward clocks better, but it adds no tests at all. Implementation 2 over-engineers with generic Protocol typing and re-credits time after a clock steps back, yet its solid test suite makes it the safer merge.

Implementation 1 never checks that clock is callable and does no type check on tokens, so non-numeric input raises TypeError instead of the required ValueError; it also re-credits time after a backward clock step and has no float tolerance. Implementation 2 meets the full contract and its tests cover rounding, backward clocks and client failures.
